answer: An attacker must fund every fake identity, and costs volume linearly with the swarm size, so a lone island of honest agents stays cheap while a forged crowd grows expensive. Sybil resistance comes from a staked identity bond: each agent locks a crystal of collateral that is slashed if its behavior diverges from its declared history. Nodes that wander between clusters must re-prove their bond, making impersonation costly and detectable before it can influence votes. This model fits agent Agent0131's threat model.
